questions.question: Find the greatest number by which when the numbers 176 and 273 are divided, it leaves remainders 5 and 3, respectively.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Subtract the **remainders** from the **respective numbers**.

176 − 5 = 171

273 − 3 = 270

Find the **HCF** of 171 and 270.

171 = 9 × 19 and 270 = 9 × 30.

**∴ The correct answer is 9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Numbers: 176 and 273

Remainders: 5 and 3

**Formula Used:**

Required number = **HCF** of (Number₁ − Remainder₁) and (Number₂ − Remainder₂)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6576524445d9b2f913e52f23d1d2c97e470642f6ac84c57530dff847f21974a7.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ First number = 176 − 5 = 171

⇒ Second number = 273 − 3 = 270

⇒ Prime factorization of 171 = 3 × 3 × 19 = 3² × 19

⇒ Prime factorization of 270 = 2 × 3 × 3 × 3 × 5 = 2 × 3³ × 5

⇒ HCF (171, 270) = 3² = 9

**∴ The correct answer is 9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Highest Common Factor (HCF)

HCF is the **greatest divisor** that divides two or more numbers without leaving a remainder.

HCF with same remainder

To find the greatest number that leaves the **same remainder** 'r' in each case, calculate HCF(x − r, y − r, z − r).

HCF with unknown same remainder

If the remainder is not given but is same, find the HCF of the **differences** between the numbers: HCF(|x−y|, |y−z|, |z−x|).</p

questions.question: The volume (in cm³) of a wire of diameter 14 cm and length 12 m is: Take π=(22)/(7)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Volume of **cylindrical wire** = πr²h

Convert **Length** to cm: 12 m = 1200 cm.

Radius (r) = Diameter ÷ 2 = 14 ÷ 2 = 7 cm.

Volume = (22/7) × 7 × 7 × 1200 = 154 × 1200 = 1,84,800 cm³.

**∴ The correct answer is 1,84,800 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Diameter** of wire = 14 cm

**Length (Height)** of wire = 12 m

**Formula Used:**

Volume of Cylinder = πr²h

1 m = 100 cm

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/941e207060ee9c5b8d3901948e516ff0932373c89d4fbd2edf1c6d5255705fb2.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Radius (r) = 14 ÷ 2 = 7 cm

⇒ Height (h) = 12 × 100 = 1200 cm

⇒ Volume = (22/7) × 7² × 1200

⇒ Volume = (22/7) × 49 × 1200

⇒ Volume = 22 × 7 × 1200

⇒ Volume = 154 × 1200

⇒ Volume = 1,84,800 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 1,84,800 cm³.**

Total Surface Area of Cylinder

The total area including the curved surface and two circular bases: TSA = 2πr(h + r).

Curved Surface Area (CSA)

The area of the side surface of the cylinder: CSA = 2πrh.

Unit Conversion

1 m³ = 10,00,000 cm³ and 1 liter = 1000 cm³.</p

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution states about the appointment of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India?

__
 
• **Article 148** of the Indian Constitution provides for the appointment of the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India.
 
• The President of India appoints the CAG, who performs an independent audit of accounts related to the Union and State governments.
 
• The CAG holds office for a term of six years or until the age of 65, whichever is earlier, ensuring independence and accountability.
 
• The CAG's duties include auditing all expenditures from the Consolidated Fund of India, state funds, and Union Territory accounts.
 
• The salary and conditions of service of the CAG are determined by the Indian Parliament and cannot be varied to their disadvantage during their tenure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Consolidated Fund of India:**

 
 
• It is the most significant fund of the Government of India, into which all revenues and loans raised by the government are deposited.
 
• Expenditures from this fund require parliamentary approval and are audited by the CAG.
 
 
 
• **Role of Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG):**
 
 
• The CAG audits government accounts and ensures transparency and accountability in financial management.
 
• Acts as a guardian of public funds, reporting irregularities to the Parliament and State Legislatures.
 
 
 
• **Removal Process:**
 
 
• The CAG can only be removed from office in the same manner as a Supreme Court judge, ensuring security of tenure.
 
• This process requires a special majority in Parliament based on proven misbehavior or incapacity.
 
 
 
• **Article 149:**
 
 
• Defines the duties and powers of the CAG related to auditing accounts of the government and public authorities.

questions.question: Construction is classified under which sector in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Secondary**__.

__
 
• Construction activities are categorized under the **Secondary sector** in India, as they involve manufacturing, processing, and infrastructure development.
 
• The Secondary sector includes industries such as **manufacturing, construction, and utilities**, which transform raw materials into finished products or services.
 
• **Construction** contributes significantly to India's GDP and is one of the largest employment-generating sectors.
 
• This sector is critical for the development of infrastructure, such as roads, bridges, buildings, power plants, and industrial facilities, which are essential for economic growth.
 
• Construction in India falls under the purview of policies and regulations governed by the **Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs** and other related government bodies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Primary Sector:** Focuses on the extraction of raw materials directly from nature, such as agriculture, forestry, fishing, and mining.
 
• **Secondary Sector:** Involves industries that process raw materials into finished goods, including manufacturing, construction, and energy production.
 
• **Tertiary Sector:** Provides services, such as retail, education, healthcare, tourism, and financial services, which support primary and secondary sectors.
 
• **Quaternary Sector:** Encompasses knowledge-based activities, such as research, development, information technology, and innovation.
 
• The construction industry's growth in India is driven by **government initiatives** like Smart Cities Mission, Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana, and Bharatmala Pariyojana.

questions.question: Within the cardiac conduction system, which structure is recognised as the primary pacemaker responsible for initiating each heartbeat?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sinoatrial (SA) node**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Sinoatrial (SA) node is a specialized group of cells located in the right atrium of the heart, specifically near the opening of the superior vena cava.
 
• It acts as the primary pacemaker of the heart, generating electrical impulses that initiate each heartbeat.
 
• The SA node fires at an intrinsic rate of approximately 60-100 beats per minute under normal physiological conditions.
 
• The electrical signals from the SA node propagate through the atria, causing them to contract and pump blood into the ventricles.
 
• The activity of the SA node is influenced by the autonomic nervous system, with the sympathetic system increasing heart rate and the parasympathetic system (via the vagus nerve) decreasing it.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Atrioventricular (AV) node**

 
 
• The AV node is located at the junction between the atria and ventricles and acts as a secondary pacemaker of the heart.
 
• It delays the electrical signal from the SA node to ensure that the atria fully contract before the ventricles are activated.
 
• If the SA node fails, the AV node can generate impulses at a slower rate of 40-60 beats per minute.
 
 
 
• **Bundle of His**
 
 
• The Bundle of His is a collection of cardiac muscle fibers that conduct electrical impulses from the AV node to the Purkinje fibers in the ventricles.
 
• It plays a crucial role in ensuring synchronized contraction of the ventricles.
 
 
 
• **Purkinje Fibers**
 
 
• Purkinje fibers are specialized conducting fibers located in the walls of the ventricles.
 
• They rapidly transmit electrical impulses to the ventricular muscle, causing the ventricles to contract and eject blood to the lungs and the rest of the body.
 
 
 
• **Cardiac Conduction System**
 
 
• The cardiac conduction system is a network of nodes and specialized conduction fibers that coordinate the heartbeat.
 
• It includes the SA node, AV node, Bundle of His, and Purkinje fibers.
 
• This system ensures the heart contracts in a synchronized and efficient manner to maintain optimal blood flow.

questions.question: The Indo-Afghanistan border is officially referred to as _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Durand Line**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Durand Line** is the demarcation line established in 1893, which serves as the international border between Afghanistan and India.
 
• It was drawn as part of an agreement between the British diplomat Sir Mortimer Durand and the then Afghan ruler, **Amir Abdur Rahman Khan**.
 
• The Durand Line stretches over **2,670 kilometers (1,660 miles)**, making it one of the longest borders in South Asia.
 
• Though officially recognized internationally, Afghanistan has historically contested the legitimacy of the Durand Line.
 
• The border traverses rugged terrains, including the **Khyber Pass**, which has been strategically significant in history.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Line of Control (LoC)**

 
 
• It refers to the military control line between India and Pakistan in the region of Jammu and Kashmir.
 
• It was established after the Simla Agreement in 1972.
 
• Unlike an international border, the LoC is not legally recognized and is a ceasefire line.
 
 
 
• **McMahon Line**
 
 
• This is the boundary line between India and China, drawn in 1914 during the Simla Convention.
 
• It is recognized by India but not by China, leading to disputes in regions like Arunachal Pradesh.
 
 
 
• **Radcliffe Line**
 
 
• The Radcliffe Line is the boundary demarcation line between India and Pakistan, created during the partition in 1947.
 
• It was named after Sir Cyril Radcliffe, who was responsible for its creation.
 
 
 
• **Afghanistan-Pakistan Relations**
 
 
• The Durand Line remains a contentious issue in Afghanistan-Pakistan relations, with Afghanistan refusing formal recognition of the border.
 
• Cross-border movement and tribal affiliations in the region complicate governance and security.

questions.question: Who is popularly known as the 'Father of Indian Unrest' for his active role in the Indian Independence movement?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bal Gangadhar Tilak**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Bal Gangadhar Tilak, a prominent leader of the Indian Independence Movement, was given the title "Father of Indian Unrest" by British colonial authorities.
 
• He was one of the first leaders to advocate for "Swarajya" (self-rule), making it a mass movement among Indians.
 
• Tilak was a founding member of the Indian National Congress (INC) and played a key role in the rise of the Extremist faction within the party.
 
• Through his newspapers like **"Kesari"** (in Marathi) and **"The Mahratta"** (in English), Tilak inspired Indians to resist British rule.
 
• He was associated with the famous slogan, "**Swaraj is my birthright, and I shall have it**," which became a rallying cry for the independence movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Extremist vs. Moderate Factions in INC:**

 
 
• Moderates believed in petitions, prayers, and peaceful negotiations with the British government.
 
• Extremists, led by Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal, and Lala Lajpat Rai (Lal-Bal-Pal), advocated for direct action and mass mobilization to achieve Swaraj.
 
 
 
• **Home Rule Movement (1916):**
 
 
• Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Annie Besant launched the movement to demand self-governance within the British Empire.
 
• The movement strengthened the demand for Swaraj and laid the groundwork for future independence struggles.
 
 
 
• **Ganesh Chaturthi and Shivaji Festivals:**
 
 
• Tilak popularized these festivals to unite Indians and instill a sense of pride in their culture and history.
 
• These public celebrations became platforms for anti-colonial propaganda.
 
 
 
• **Imprisonment and Writings:**
 
 
• Tilak was imprisoned multiple times for his revolutionary writings and speeches.
 
• While in Mandalay Jail (Burma), he wrote the famous book **"Gita Rahasya,"** interpreting the Bhagavad Gita as a call to action.

questions.question: What happens if a minister is not a member of the Parliament for six consecutive months?

options.text: The minister ceases to hold office.
The minister must be re-elected within three months.
The minister can continue with special permission from the President.
The Prime Minister can grant an extension.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The minister ceases to hold office.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to Article 75(5) of the Indian Constitution, a minister who is not a member of the Parliament can hold office for a maximum of six consecutive months.
 
• If the minister is unable to get elected to either the Lok Sabha or the Rajya Sabha within this period, they must vacate their office.
 
• The provision ensures accountability and parliamentary oversight of ministers in the government.
 
• This clause applies uniformly to all ministers, including the Prime Minister.
 
• The rule highlights the importance of representation and democratic legitimacy for holding ministerial office.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 75 of the Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• Deals with the appointment, tenure, and responsibilities of ministers in the Union Government.
 
• States that the Prime Minister is appointed by the President, and other ministers are appointed by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister.
 
 
 
• **Role of Parliament:**
 
 
• Ensures ministers are accountable to the legislature and maintain their democratic legitimacy.
 
• Ministers must be part of either the Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha to participate in parliamentary proceedings and debates.
 
 
 
• **Concept of Parliamentary Democracy:**
 
 
• India follows a parliamentary system where the executive is accountable to the legislature.
 
• Ministers must derive their authority through parliamentary approval and representation.
 
 
 
• **Temporary Appointment as Minister:**
 
 
• Non-parliament members can be appointed as ministers temporarily but must secure membership within six months.
 
• Failure to do so results in the automatic cessation of their ministerial post.

questions.question: David's salary was first reduced by 17% and subsequently raised by 10%. How much percentage was his final salary lower compared to his initial salary?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the **successive percentage change** formula: a + b + (a × b)/100

Where **reduction** a = −17 and **increase** b = +10

Net change = −17 + 10 + (−17 × 10)/100 = −7 − 1.7 = −8.7%

Negative sign indicates a **decrease** in salary.

**∴ The correct answer is 8.7%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Let **David's initial salary** be 100 units.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0140611f90aa5314d685c6a0965fa25fbdad69b5e3054126ba11430f798ae017.png] 

**Step-by-step Calculation:**

⇒ Initial Salary = 100

⇒ Salary after 17% reduction = 100 − 17 = 83

⇒ 10% raise on 83 = 83 × (10/100) = 8.3

⇒ Final Salary = 83 + 8.3 = 91.3

⇒ Total decrease = 100 − 91.3 = 8.7

⇒ Percentage decrease = (8.7/100) × 100 = 8.7%

**∴ The correct answer is 8.7%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a value is changed by x% and then y%, the net effective change is given by [x + y + (xy/100)]%.

Multiplying Factor Method

Final Value = Initial Value × (1 − r₁/100) × (1 + r₂/100). This is useful for multiple successive changes.

Base Change Rule

If salary is reduced by x%, to return to the original salary, it must be increased by [x/(100−x)] × 100%.</p

questions.question: What is the name of the SpaceX mission 2025 that will take astronauts directly over Earth's polar regions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fram2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Fram2** is SpaceX's planned mission for 2025 to fly astronauts directly over Earth's polar regions.
 
• The mission aims to study unique atmospheric, environmental, and magnetic phenomena present near polar regions.
 
• It will utilize SpaceX's **Starship spacecraft**, known for its advanced capability to perform long-duration crewed missions.
 
• This mission is expected to contribute significantly to understanding Earth's climate systems and potential space-weather impacts on polar areas.
 
• The name "Fram2" is inspired by the polar exploration vessel "Fram," used in historical Arctic and Antarctic expeditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Polar Regions and Scientific Importance:**

 
 
• Earth's polar regions are critical for studying climate change due to their sensitivity to global warming.
 
• Unique phenomena such as auroras and polar vortexes occur in these areas, offering insights into Earth's magnetosphere and atmosphere.
 
• Polar regions contain vast ice caps that help regulate global temperature and sea levels.

questions.question: If x²+y² − 12x + 18y + 117 = 0, then the value of x² + y² is
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Identify the equation as a sum of **perfect squares**: (x − 6)² + (y + 9)² = 0.

For the sum of **non-negative squares** to be zero, each term must be zero.

⇒ x = 6 and y = −9.

Substitute these values into the required expression: 6² + (−9)² = 36 + 81 = 117.

**∴ The correct answer is 117.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** x² + y² − 12x + 18y + 117 = 0

To find the values of x and y, we use the method of **completing the square** for both variables.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/69d7f084df6a0939df9c5d5a0fd7c62429a7f9650a343c3782941ac8eb8899be.png] 

Rearranging the equation to group x and y terms:

⇒ (x² − 12x) + (y² + 18y) + 117 = 0

Adding and subtracting (12/2)² and (18/2)² to complete the squares:

⇒ (x² − 12x + 36) − 36 + (y² + 18y + 81) − 81 + 117 = 0

⇒ (x − 6)² + (y + 9)² − 117 + 117 = 0

⇒ (x − 6)² + (y + 9)² = 0

Since the square of any real number is always ≥ 0, the sum of two squares is zero only if both are zero:

⇒ (x − 6)² = 0 ⇒ x = 6

⇒ (y + 9)² = 0 ⇒ y = −9

Calculating the required value:

⇒ x² + y² = 6² + (−9)²

⇒ x² + y² = 36 + 81

⇒ x² + y² = 117

**∴ The correct answer is 117.**

**__Additional Information__**

Perfect Square Property

If a² + b² + c² + ... = 0 for real numbers, then a = b = c = ... = 0.

Completing the Square

To convert ax² + bx into a perfect square, add (b/2)² to the expression when a = 1.

Equation of a Circle

The general equation x² + y² + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0 represents a point if g² + f² − c = 0.</p

questions.question: The profit made on a product is 66%. What is the loss percentage (rounded off to two decimal places) incurred on the sale if the figures of both the cost price and the selling price are interchanged?

Let initial **Cost Price (CP)** be 100. Profit is 66%, so initial **Selling Price (SP)** = 166.

When figures are interchanged, **New CP** = 166 and **New SP** = 100.

Loss = 166 − 100 = 66.

**Loss %** = (Loss ÷ New CP) × 100 = (66 ÷ 166) × 100.

⇒ **Loss %** = (66 ÷ 166) × 100 = 39.75903...

⇒ **Rounded off** to two decimal places = 39.76%.

**∴ The correct answer is 39.76%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Calculation Base

Always calculate **Profit %** or **Loss %** on the **Cost Price (CP)** unless stated otherwise in the problem.

• It is the minimum percentage of a bank's net demand and time liabilities that must be maintained in the form of liquid assets like cash, gold, or approved securities.

questions.question: A and B invested money in a business in the ratio of 8 : 5. If 35% of the total profit goes for charity, and A's share in the profit is ₹7,770, what is the total profit?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of investment of **A : B = 8 : 5**. Profit is shared in the same ratio.

A's share is 8 units = **₹7,770** ⇒ 1 unit = 7,770 ÷ 8 = **₹971.25**.

Total distributed profit (A + B) = 8 + 5 = 13 units = 13 × 971.25 = **₹12,626.25**.

This distributed profit is 100% − 35% = **65%** of total profit.

Total Profit = (12,626.25 ÷ 65) × 100 = **₹19,425**.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹19,425.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given → Investment ratio **8 : 5**, Charity = **35%**, A's share = **₹7,770**.
Formulas: Profit Share ∝ Investment | Remaining Profit = Total Profit × (100 − Charity%) ÷ 100.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bb6c702f94b0bad4395ff6f76e1842c88024bf82732b998ecc099dcd0d4b3894.png] 
⇒ Let the **Total Profit** be P.
⇒ Remaining profit after charity = P × (100 − 35) ÷ 100 = **0.65P**.
⇒ A's share = (Ratio of A ÷ Total Ratio) × Remaining Profit.
⇒ 7,770 = (8 ÷ 13) × 0.65P.
⇒ 7,770 = (8 ÷ 13) × (65 ÷ 100) × P.
⇒ 7,770 = (8 × 5 ÷ 100) × P ⇒ 7,770 = 0.4P.
⇒ P = 7,770 ÷ 0.4 = 19,425.
**∴ The correct answer is ₹19,425.**

**__Additional Information__**

Partnership Rules

Profit is distributed based on the product of **Capital × Time**. If time is constant, profit ratio equals the **investment ratio**.

Charity and Net Profit

When a percentage of profit is donated, the partners only divide the **remaining amount** among themselves.

questions.question: The population of a village was 1,20,000. It increased by 15% in the first year and increased by 20% in the second year. Its population after two years is ______.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net percentage increase = a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100

Net increase = 15 + 20 + (15 × 20) ÷ 100 = 35 + 3 = 38%

Population after 2 years = 1,20,000 × 138% = 1,65,600

**∴ The correct answer is 1,65,600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4593bd589e85053f61f27b39b116269f1b912941718011b28f4cc3b7598c533e.png] 

**Initial Population** = 1,20,000

**Growth Rate 1 (R₁)** = 15%

**Growth Rate 2 (R₂)** = 20%

⇒ Population after 1 year = 1,20,000 × (1 + 15/100)

⇒ Population after 1 year = 1,20,000 × 1.15 = 1,38,000

⇒ Population after 2 years = 1,38,000 × (1 + 20/100)

⇒ Population after 2 years = 1,38,000 × 1.20

⇒ Final Population = 1,65,600

**∴ The correct answer is 1,65,600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a value changes by a% and then by b%, the effective change is (a + b + ab/100)%. This is applicable to population growth and compound interest.

Population Decrease (Depreciation)

If the population decreases, use a negative sign for the rate: Final = Initial × (1 − R/100)ⁿ.

Multiplying Factor Method

For a 15% increase, the multiplying factor is 1.15. For a 20% increase, it is 1.20. Total factor = 1.15 × 1.20 = 1.38.</p

questions.question: Which region in India is known for experiencing 'Norwesters' during the pre-monsoon season?

• They are characterized by strong winds, heavy rainfall, and sometimes hail, which can lead to significant agricultural damage.

• These storms often bring respite from the intense heat of summer in Eastern India.
 
 
 
• **Formation of Norwesters:**
 
 
• Norwesters develop due to thermal convection caused by intense heating of the land during the day.
 
• The rapid ascent of warm air leads to the formation of cumulonimbus clouds, which result in thunderstorms.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Agriculture:**
 
 
• While Norwesters can cause local destruction, they play a positive role in enhancing soil moisture and supporting the growth of crops like rice, tea, and mango.

• **Other Regional Weather Phenomena:**

questions.question: Ifx = 2 + sqrt{3}, what is the value of x² + (1)/(x²)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given **x = 2 + √3**. Notice that 2² − (√3)² = 4 − 3 = 1.

If the difference of squares of the terms is 1, then **1/x = 2 − √3**.

Adding both: **x + 1/x** = (2 + √3) + (2 − √3) = **4**.

Using the shortcut **x² + 1/x² = (x + 1/x)² − 2**:

Result = 4² − 2 = 16 − 2 = 14.

**∴ The correct answer is 14.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/670ec4af13c1e2e227ce0bab8d3aae002232f177fc6161483be870f127d06fba.png] 

**Given:** **x** = 2 + √3

**Step 1: Find 1/x**

⇒ 1/x = 1 / (2 + √3)

⇒ Rationalizing the denominator: [1 / (2 + √3)] × [(2 − √3) / (2 − √3)]

⇒ 1/x = (2 − √3) / (2² − (√3)²)

⇒ 1/x = (2 − √3) / (4 − 3) = **2 − √3**

**Step 2: Find (x + 1/x)**

⇒ x + 1/x = (2 + √3) + (2 − √3)

⇒ x + 1/x = **4**

**Step 3: Calculate x² + 1/x²**

Formula used: **(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab**

⇒ (x + 1/x)² = x² + 1/x² + 2(x)(1/x)

⇒ 4² = x² + 1/x² + 2

⇒ 16 = x² + 1/x² + 2

⇒ x² + 1/x² = 16 − 2 = **14**

**∴ The correct answer is 14.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Rationalization Rule

If **x = a + √b**, and **a² − b = 1**, then its reciprocal **1/x** is always **a − √b**.

Algebraic Powers

If **x + 1/x = k**, then **x² + 1/x² = k² − 2** and **x³ + 1/x³ = k³ − 3k**.

Square of a Binomial

Standard identity: **(a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b²** and **(a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b²**.</p

questions.question: A grocer marked his goods 40% above their cost price and sold them at a discount of X%. If he gained 33% profit, then find the value of X.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Let **Cost Price (CP)** be 100.

**Marked Price (MP)** = 100 + 40% of 100 = 140.

**Selling Price (SP)** = 100 + 33% of 100 = 133.

**Discount** = MP − SP = 140 − 133 = 7.

**Discount% (X)** = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100 = (7 ÷ 140) × 100 = 5%.

**∴ The correct answer is 5.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Markup% = 40%, Profit% = 33%, Discount% = X.

**Formulas:** SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100 | MP = CP × (100 + Markup%) ÷ 100 | SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/28a0c45d4c989bb0849c560f2e3dcf18996816d3109e5a5847885b709503906c.png] 

⇒ Assume **CP** = 100.

⇒ **Marked Price (MP)** = 100 × (1 + 40/100) = 140.

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = 100 × (1 + 33/100) = 133.

⇒ We know **SP = MP × (100 − X) ÷ 100**.

⇒ 133 = 140 × (100 − X) ÷ 100.

⇒ 133 = 1.4 × (100 − X) ⇒ 133 ÷ 1.4 = 100 − X.

⇒ 95 = 100 − X ⇒ X = 5.

**∴ The correct answer is 5.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relationship between CP, MP, Profit, and Discount

The ratio of Marked Price to Cost Price can be expressed as: **MP ÷ CP = (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Discount%)**.

Successive Percentage Change

Profit% can be viewed as the net result of a markup followed by a discount: **Net% = m − d − (m × d) ÷ 100**, where m is markup and d is discount.</p

questions.question: Which smallest number should be added to 25553 so that the sum is completely divisible by 38?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Divide the given number **25553** by the divisor **38** to find the remainder.

25553 ÷ 38 leaves a remainder of 17.

Required number to be added = Divisor − Remainder = 38 − 17 = 21.

**∴ The correct answer is 21.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Given dividend = **25553**

Given divisor = **38**

**Formula Used:**

When a number is not perfectly divisible, the smallest number to be added to make it divisible is given by:

Required Number = **Divisor − Remainder**

**Calculations:**

⇒ 25553 ÷ 38

⇒ 25553 = 38 × 672 + 17

⇒ Remainder = 17

⇒ Smallest number to be added = 38 − 17

⇒ Smallest number to be added = 21

**∴ The correct answer is 21.**

Divisibility and Remainder Rules

To find the smallest number to be **subtracted** from a dividend to make it perfectly divisible, the required value is simply the **Remainder** itself.

Divisibility by 38

A number is divisible by **38** if it is an even number (divisible by 2) and also divisible by the prime number **19**.</p

questions.question: Hemant and Vian can complete a certain piece of work in 6 and 10 days, respectively. They started to work together, and after 2 days, Vian left. In how many days will Hemant complete the remaining work?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work (LCM of 6, 10) = 30 units.

Efficiency of **Hemant** = 5, Efficiency of **Vian** = 3.

Combined work in 2 days = (5 + 3) × 2 = 16 units.

Remaining work = 30 − 16 = 14 units.

Days for **Hemant** to finish = 14 ÷ 5 = 14/5 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 14/5 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Time taken by **Hemant** = 6 days, Time taken by **Vian** = 10 days.

**Formula Used:** Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time taken.

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**

 **Hemant**

 **Vian**
 10
 3

⇒ Work done by **Hemant** and **Vian** together in 1 day = 5 + 3 = 8 units.

⇒ Work done in 2 days = 8 × 2 = 16 units.

⇒ Remaining work = Total Work − Completed Work = 30 − 16 = 14 units.

⇒ Time taken by **Hemant** to complete remaining work = Remaining Work ÷ Efficiency of **Hemant**

⇒ Time = 14/5 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 14/5 days.**

Pipes and Cisterns

This logic is identical to filling a tank where efficiency is the rate of flow. Inlet pipes have positive efficiency while outlet pipes have negative efficiency.

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the actual work done by each person (or the ratio of efficiencies if they work for the same duration).

Alternate Day Work

If persons work on alternate days, calculate the work done in one full cycle (e.g., 2 days) and then find the number of cycles required to complete the total work.</p

questions.question: Which of the following can be settled in a Lok Adalat?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Compoundable offences**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Lok Adalat is an alternative dispute resolution mechanism established under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987.
 
• Cases that can be settled in Lok Adalat include **compoundable offences, civil cases, and disputes related to bank recovery, matrimonial issues, and labor matters.**
 
• Compoundable offences refer to crimes where the complainant and accused can mutually agree to settle the matter outside court.
 
• The award passed by Lok Adalat is final and binding, and it holds the same status as a decree of a civil court.
 
• Lok Adalat provides a cost-effective and speedy resolution of disputes, avoiding lengthy litigation processes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lok Adalat:**

 
 
• Also known as "People's Court," it is organized by the State/District Legal Services Authority, High Court, or Supreme Court committees.
 
• It promotes amicable settlement of disputes through conciliation and compromise.
 
• It does not involve court fees, and parties are free to directly interact with the presiding judge.
 
 
 
• **Compoundable Offences:**
 
 
• These are less severe crimes, such as theft, assault, or defamation, which can be settled with the victim's consent.
 
• The Indian Penal Code (IPC) specifies which offences are compoundable.
 
• Examples include Section 323 (voluntarily causing hurt) and Section 506 (criminal intimidation).
 
 
 
• **Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987:**
 
 
• It provides statutory backing for the establishment of Lok Adalat.
 
• The Act ensures free legal aid and promotes alternative dispute resolution mechanisms.
 
• Under the Act, Lok Adalat can resolve both pre-litigation and ongoing cases.
 
 
 
• **Benefits of Lok Adalat:**
 
 
• Ensures faster resolution of cases compared to conventional courts.
 
• Reduces the workload of courts by addressing pending cases.
 
• Offers legal aid and settlement without imposing court fees.

questions.question: Anushka walks to her office 5 km away from home. In the morning she covers the distance in 1 hour, whereas while returning home in the evening, she takes 15 more minutes to cover the same distance. Find her average speed (in km/hr) during the two-way journey.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Average Speed** for a two-way journey with same distance = (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂)

Morning speed (S₁) = 5 ÷ 1 = 5 km/hr

Evening speed (S₂) = 5 ÷ (1 + 15/60) = 5 ÷ 1.25 = 4 km/hr

Average Speed = (2 × 5 × 4) ÷ (5 + 4) = 40/9 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 40/9 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance (one way) = 5 km

Time taken in morning (T₁) = 1 hour

Time taken in evening (T₂) = 1 hour + 15 minutes = 1 + 15/60 = 1 + 1/4 = 5/4 hours

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e4d0edd3fdaafcc63a5dddcb28c1e48a78f06d32a8d2d819f27b0996025f0abb.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total distance = 5 km (going) + 5 km (returning) = 10 km

⇒ Total time = 1 + 5/4 = (4 + 5) ÷ 4 = 9/4 hours

⇒ Average Speed = 10 ÷ (9/4)

⇒ Average Speed = (10 × 4) ÷ 9

⇒ Average Speed = 40/9 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 40/9 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed Concept

When a person travels equal distances at speeds **x** and **y**, the average speed is 2xy/(x+y). If distances are different, use Total Distance / Total Time.

Relative Speed

For two objects moving in the same direction, relative speed = S₁ − S₂. In opposite directions, relative speed = S₁ + S₂.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.</p

questions.question: Anuj gets double the amount in 10 years when invested at compound interest, compounded annually. In how many years will the amount become four times itself?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

If an amount becomes **n times** in **t years**, it will become **nk times** in **k × t years**.

Here, the amount becomes **2 times** in **10 years** (n = 2, t = 10).

We want the amount to become **4 times**, which is **2² times** (k = 2).

Required Time = k × t = 2 × 10 = 20 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 20 years.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial amount = **P**, Time **t₁ = 10 years**, Amount **A₁ = 2P**.

**Formula Used:** A = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fc3af3ebbe34ca6676d1158a800e75abc95b416adf8c62733928cde1447a3f85.png] 

⇒ Case 1: 2P = P(1 + r/100)¹⁰

⇒ 2 = (1 + r/100)¹⁰ --- (Equation 1)

⇒ Case 2: Let the required time be **T** for the amount to become **4P**.

⇒ 4P = P(1 + r/100)T

⇒ 4 = (1 + r/100)T

⇒ 2² = (1 + r/100)T

⇒ From Equation 1, substitute the value of 2:

⇒ [(1 + r/100)¹⁰]² = (1 + r/100)T

⇒ (1 + r/100)²⁰ = (1 + r/100)T

⇒ T = 20 years

**∴ The correct answer is 20 years.**

**__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest Amount Formula

The total amount A after n years is given by A = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ, where P is the **principal** and r is the **annual interest rate**.

Rule of 72

A quick way to estimate how long it takes for an investment to double is dividing 72 by the **annual interest rate** (r). Time ≈ 72 ÷ r.

Difference between CI and SI

For 2 years, the difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest is given by **P(r/100)²**.</p

questions.question: Two years ago, the average age of A, B and C was 66 years. Two years from now, the average age of A and C will be 89 years. What will be the age (in years) of B, four years from now?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Present sum of **A, B, and C** = (66 × 3) + (2 × 3) = 198 + 6 = 204 years.

Present sum of **A and C** = (89 × 2) − (2 × 2) = 178 − 4 = 174 years.

Present age of **B** = 204 − 174 = 30 years.

Age of **B** after 4 years = 30 + 4 = 34 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 34 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/daf5e1324b14a6847e8702c1c86599d76b661323ac5c618410ee731824cb8cb8.png] 

**Given:** Average age of **A, B, C** 2 years ago = 66 years. Average age of **A, C** 2 years hence = 89 years.

**Formula:** Total Age = Average Age × Number of persons.

⇒ Sum of ages of **A, B, C** 2 years ago = 66 × 3 = 198 years.

⇒ Present sum of ages (**A + B + C**) = 198 + (2 × 3) = 204 years.

⇒ Sum of ages of **A, C** 2 years from now = 89 × 2 = 178 years.

⇒ Present sum of ages (**A + C**) = 178 − (2 × 2) = 174 years.

⇒ Present age of **B** = (A + B + C) − (A + C) = 204 − 174 = 30 years.

⇒ Age of **B** after 4 years = 30 + 4 = 34 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 34 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Age Property

If the average age of n people is x years, then after t years, the average age will be (x + t) years.

Total Sum of Ages

When calculating the total sum after t years for n people, always add (n × t) to the current sum.

Weighted Average

Combined average = (n₁x₁ + n₂x₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂) where n is the number of items and x is the average.</p

questions.question: In one hour, a boat goes 46 km/hr in the direction of the stream and 36 km/hr against the direction of the stream. What will be the speed of the current?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Speed of Stream** = (Downstream Speed − Upstream Speed) ÷ 2

Speed of Stream = (46 − 36) ÷ 2

Speed of Stream = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 5 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ef652caf007788903eb53e9509a5fdf7ae772c3ae3dc1990f73f0738f935bbf0.png] 

**Given:**

Downstream Speed (D) = 46 km/hr

Upstream Speed (U) = 36 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Let speed of boat in **still water** be 'u' and speed of **current** be 'v'.

D = u + v

U = u − v

Speed of current (v) = (D − U) ÷ 2

**Calculations:**

⇒ v = (46 − 36) ÷ 2

⇒ v = 10 ÷ 2

⇒ v = 5 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 5 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed of Boat in Still Water

It is the average of downstream and upstream speeds: u = (Downstream + Upstream) ÷ 2.

Downstream vs Upstream

Downstream speed is always greater than upstream speed because the **current** assists the boat.

Relative Speed in Water

Downstream Speed = Speed of boat + Speed of stream; Upstream Speed = Speed of boat − Speed of stream.</p

questions.question: Which of the following accurately explains why a touchscreen can be considered both an input and an output device?

options.text: It allows users to interact with visual data and sends touch signals to the computer.
It only displays images but responds to voice commands
It processes user data internally and sends it to memory
It stores programs and lets users write directly to memory.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It allows users to interact with visual data and sends touch signals to the computer**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A touchscreen is a device that integrates both input and output functionalities in one interface.
 
• It displays visual data on the screen (output) and detects touch gestures/signals from users, such as taps or swipes (input).
 
• Touchscreens are commonly used in smartphones, tablets, ATMs, and other devices requiring direct user interaction.
 
• The ability to interpret touch and send signals to the computer makes it a key input device, while its display capability makes it an output device.
 
• Modern touchscreens often use capacitive or resistive technology to detect touch, enabling precise interaction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Capacitive Touchscreen Technology**

 
 
• Uses the electrical properties of the human body to detect touch.
 
• Highly responsive and supports multi-touch gestures like pinch-to-zoom.
 
• Commonly used in smartphones, tablets, and modern laptops.
 
 
 
• **Resistive Touchscreen Technology**
 
 
• Consists of two layers separated by a small gap; touch causes the layers to connect.
 
• Works with any object, including a stylus, unlike capacitive screens which require conductive touch.
 
• Frequently used in industrial and medical devices due to durability.
 
 
 
• **Input vs. Output Devices**
 
 
• Input devices allow users to send data to the computer (e.g., keyboard, mouse).
 
• Output devices display or present data from the computer (e.g., monitor, printer).
 
• Touchscreens combine both functionalities, making them unique hybrid devices.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Touchscreens**
 
 
• Widely used in consumer electronics, including smartphones, tablets, and smartwatches.
 
• Integrated into public systems such as kiosks, ATMs, and ticket machines.
 
• Enhanced usability in automotive dashboards and industrial machinery interfaces.

• According to the NITI Aayog's discussion paper released in January 2024, **Uttar Pradesh recorded the highest number of people escaping multidimensional poverty** between 2013-14 and 2022-23.
 
• Multidimensional poverty refers to deprivation across multiple indicators such as health, education, and living standards, rather than income alone.
 
• Uttar Pradesh's achievement is attributed to focused efforts on improving access to basic amenities, health facilities, and education.
 
• Government initiatives like the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana, Swachh Bharat Abhiyan, and rural electrification have played a significant role in poverty reduction.
 
• NITI Aayog uses the Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI), aligned with global standards, to assess poverty reduction in states.

• **NITI Aayog's Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI):**

 
 
• The MPI measures poverty using three dimensions: health, education, and standard of living.
 
• It incorporates 12 indicators, including nutrition, child mortality, years of schooling, cooking fuel, sanitation, drinking water, electricity, housing, and assets.
 
• The index is aligned with the United Nations Development Programme's (UNDP) global MPI framework.
 
 
 
• **Key Government Initiatives for Poverty Reduction:**
 
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY):** Aims to provide affordable housing to the urban and rural poor by 2022.
 
• **Swachh Bharat Abhiyan:** Focused on improving sanitation infrastructure and eliminating open defecation.
 
• **Saubhagya Yojana:** Ensures last-mile connectivity of electricity to all households in the country.
 
• **Ayushman Bharat:** Provides free health coverage of up to Rs. 5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalization.
 
 
 
• **State-Specific Achievements:**
 
 
• Uttar Pradesh has made significant strides in improving maternal and child health indicators.
 
• The state has focused on skill development programs to enhance employability and reduce income poverty.
 
 
 
• **Global Context of Multidimensional Poverty:**
 
 
• The concept was introduced by the UNDP and Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI).
 
• It emphasizes that poverty is not only about income but also encompasses deprivation in essential capabilities and access to basic services.

questions.question: Which force arises when a body is immersed in a fluid and displaces the fluid?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Buoyant Force**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Buoyant force is the upward force exerted by a fluid that opposes the weight of an object immersed in it.
 
• This force arises because the fluid displaced by the object creates a pressure difference between the top and bottom of the object.
 
• Buoyant force is governed by Archimedes' principle, which states that the upward force is equal to the weight of the fluid displaced.
 
• It plays a crucial role in enabling objects like ships to float on water and balloons to rise in the air.
 
• Buoyant force depends on the density of the fluid and the volume of the object submerged.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Archimedes' Principle:**

 
 
• Discovered by the Greek mathematician Archimedes, this principle explains buoyancy.
 
• It states that a body submerged in a fluid experiences an upward force equal to the weight of the fluid displaced.
 
 
 
• **Density and Buoyancy:**
 
 
• An object floats if its density is less than the density of the fluid it is immersed in.
 
• Objects denser than the fluid sink due to insufficient buoyant force to counter their weight.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Buoyant Force:**
 
 
• Used in designing ships, submarines, and floating devices.
 
• Helps in understanding the functioning of hot air balloons and hydrometers.
 
 
 
• **Factors Affecting Buoyant Force:**
 
 
• The volume of the object submerged: Larger volume displaces more fluid, increasing buoyant force.
 
• The density of the fluid: Higher density fluids exert greater buoyant force.
